newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to rethink Kredyt Bank request.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to rethink Kredyt Bank request.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Monday that it would reconsider an application by Poland's Kredyt Bank to establish a branch office.
The Bank of Lithuania last week rejected Kredyt Bank's request on the grounds that it failed to meet all of the criteria required to enter the Lithuanian market.
But Jonas Niaura, central bank deputy governor, told Reuters that the bank's board would reconsider Kredyt Bank's application because it was made before the requirements were established.
"Kredyt Bank applied before the criteria were set so we are prepared to make an exemption in this case," Niaura said.
"We are discussing the situation now with Kredyt bank's management," he added.

The criteria required by foreign banks who wish to enter Lithuania include a minimum capital of 50 million Ecu, two consecutive years of operating without a loss and positive ratings from Moody's, ICBA and Standard & Poors.

Kredyt Bank opened a representative office in Lithuania earlier this year and was the first foreign bank to apply for permission to open a branch after parliament passed a law in June lifting a ban on foreign banks.
The law was passed in response to a crisis which rocked Lithuania's banking sector late last year with the shock closure of two of its top banks.
